statements.worth_reason: Praise ('incredible', 'a work of love') and development-effort trivia (four years, thousands of engineering years) say nothing about volume, price or share.
statements.day_note: event_time is the report day; the article does not date the London developer event, so unknown.

statements.worth_reason: The first Microsoft device to use an NVIDIA chip (N1X / RTX Spark) is a named partner adoption marking NVIDIA's entry into Windows PC processors, which bears on its competitive position against Intel, AMD and Qualcomm (supporting weight).
statements.day_note: Revealed in September 2026 per the article; original_who is TechRadar and original_day the report day 2026-10-17 instead of Microsoft/NVIDIA and 2026-09.

statements.worth_reason: One petaflop and 'first NVIDIA GPU with shared memory' are product-specification detail with no business scale (5.3 row on product details).
statements.day_note: event_time is the report day; the article does not date Huang's remarks, so unknown.

missed.quote: But as Huang tells it, the creation of the device, set to launch on October 16 2026, was a long and arduous process.
missed.why: The launch date is the product-cycle state change (shipping from October 16, 2026) that the September reveal in e2 lacks.

grade_reason: The one useful fact (the first Microsoft device with an NVIDIA chip) is kept, but two of three records are praise or specification noise, the launch date is missed, and e2 names TechRadar on the report day as its original source.
